themes_detail.label: Encampment surge in Coney Island
themes_detail.summary: Homelessness-related encampment complaints exploded to 7 THIS WEEK—a 700% spike versus the 0.9 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks—signaling a sudden concentration of unhoused residents or failed outreach in CD 313.
evidence: 7 encampment complaints filed THIS WEEK vs. 0.9 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 6.61)
700% spike represents most acute emergence in the dataset
Timing coincides with seasonal transition; warrants investigation into shelter capacity and outreach coordination
reporting_angles: Where are encampments clustered? Map them and interview residents in adjacent blocks.
Are local shelters at capacity? Contact NYC DHS and local service providers about bed availability.
Interview unhoused individuals about why they're settling in Coney Island now—push factors from other neighborhoods?

themes_detail.label: Indoor air quality complaints spike
themes_detail.summary: Indoor Air Quality complaints jumped 250% to 7 complaints last week versus a 2.0 weekly average—potentially signaling mold, heating malfunctions, or ventilation failures affecting multiple residential units.
evidence: 7 indoor air quality complaints last week vs. 2.0 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 7.07)
250% spike overlaps with heating season onset; may be linked to HEAT/HOT WATER complaints (1022 total in 90 days)
Air quality concerns are health-critical in dense residential areas like Brighton Beach
reporting_angles: Interview tenants: are complaints clustered in specific buildings or blocks? Are landlords addressing heat + ventilation together?
Check DOB permit data (158 alterations filed in 90 days) for HVAC-related work—are contractors cutting corners?
Does HPD have open violations on buildings with air quality complaints? Cross-reference 311 data with HPD registry.

themes_detail.label: Obstruction and street sign decay accelerating
themes_detail.summary: Obstruction complaints (sidewalk/street blockages) spiked 860% to 6 last week versus 0.6 weekly average, and Street Sign damage rose 700% to 5 last week versus 0.6 average—suggesting infrastructure neglect or construction debris accumulation.
evidence: Obstruction complaints: 6 last week vs. 0.6 weekly average (z-score: 5.42)
Street Sign Damaged: 5 last week vs. 0.6 weekly average (z-score: 6.29)
Both spikes occurred last week, suggesting coordinated or cascading infrastructure issue
28 new building permits filed in 90 days—possible construction-related obstructions and damage
reporting_angles: Walk the district: photograph obstructions and damaged signs. Are they concentrated near the 2950 West 24th St rezoning or other active development sites?
Interview DOT about street sign repair backlog. How quickly are damaged signs replaced?
Cross-reference 311 obstruction complaints with active DOB permits—are construction sites violating sidewalk closure rules?

themes_detail.label: Drinking in public complaints unprecedented
themes_detail.summary: Public drinking complaints hit 4 last week—a 3100% spike from a 0.1 weekly baseline—marking an unprecedented emergence of alcohol-related street behavior that may reflect broader disorder or enforcement policy shifts.
evidence: 4 drinking complaints last week vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 11.72)
3100% spike is statistical outlier; historically rare issue in CD 313
Timing unclear—could reflect new enforcement patrols, seasonal beach tourism, or disorder clustering
reporting_angles: Has NYPD increased foot patrols or enforcement on Coney Island boardwalk or beach? Interview local precinct.
Are complaints concentrated on boardwalk vs. residential streets? Geographic clustering may indicate tourism-related behavior.
Is this tied to recent entertainment venue openings or seasonal changes? Check community board agendas for venue licensing.

themes_detail.label: Vendor enforcement complaints spike
themes_detail.summary: Unlicensed vendor complaints jumped to 4 two weeks ago—a 3100% spike from 0.1 weekly average—suggesting either enforcement crackdowns or informal street vending proliferation.
evidence: 4 vendor enforcement complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.1 weekly average (z-score: 11.72)
Spike timing suggests either coordinated NYPD/DOC crackdown or seasonal vendor migration to beachfront
Lacks recent data; incident occurred 2 weeks ago, not this week—lower recency priority
reporting_angles: Did DOC launch a vendor compliance sweep in CD 313? Request incident reports.
Interview street vendors: are they facing new enforcement, or is winter pushing them to beachfront locations?
Check previous community board meeting agendas for vendor-related complaints; this may be recurring.
